messages:
jordan (support): Customer on Private deployment (Azure Private Link + Firewall) reports intermittent 502s to our /v1/generate endpoint from one app-subnet only. They say it started after a firewall upgrade.
liam (sre): Can you share repro steps and a minimal curl stdout/stderr please? also which subnets are affected?
jordan (support): Repro steps: app in subnet app-prod-eu-1 calls api.redwood.internal -> private endpoint IP -> through AZ Firewall. curl -v shows TLS handshake then immediate HTTP/1.1 502. Example:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer XXX"
* Connected to 10.1.12.45 (10.1.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.internal
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< Content-Type: text/html
```
liam (sre): That looks like the TLS part completes then the backend returns 502. Can you paste a tcpdump around the failure (only header lines)?
jordan (support): tcpdump snip from app host:
```
12:02:11.123 IP 10.1.18.22.443 > 10.1.12.45.52134: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 1, win 0
12:02:11.123 IP 10.1.12.45.52134 > 10.1.18.22.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:233, ack 1, win 1024
```
jordan (support): openssl s_client -connect 10.1.12.45:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -showcerts gives server cert CN=api-fw-proxy.internal.azure.net (uh oh)
priya (networking): That suggests Azure Firewall or a TLS inspection proxy is terminating TLS and presenting its cert. Does the firewall have TLS inspection enabled (IDPS/DPI)?
jordan (support): Customer says they enabled TLS inspection on the firewall after upgrade. Also only calls from app-prod-eu-1 hit the path that goes through the firewall SNAT pool; app-prod-eu-2 goes via a different route and is fine.
liam (sre): Two hypotheses: 1) TLS inspection is rewriting SNI/cert and then our backend drops requests because it sees a different Host header or unexpected client IP. 2) SNAT from the firewall maps the source to an IP not in their backend allowlist -> backend rejects with 502 from internal auth. Can you check the request logs on our side with the private endpoint IP and the client port? eng-bot, pull logs for private endpoint 10.1.12.45 around 12:02.
eng-bot: pulled logs -> 2026-03-09T12:02:11Z request from 10.1.18.22:52134 -> proxied; backend returned 502 ProxyError: TLSHandshakeVerificationFailed (SNI mismatch) (trace id abc-123)
priya (networking): Also check route table for app-prod-eu-1. If forced tunneling or a user-defined route sends traffic to firewall for internet-bound, PrivateLink->Firewall interaction could break return path. run:
```
az network route-table route list --resource-group RG-prod --route-table-name rt-app-prod-eu-1
```
jordan (support): Route table shows default 0.0.0.0/0 -> azure-firewall-ip. Private endpoint subnet has no special route but the app subnet traffic to private endpoint IP walks via firewall due to NSG + UDR.
liam (sre): That's the issue: calls to the private endpoint should be direct within VNet (no UDR forcing to firewall). Forcing them through firewall causes TLS inspection and SNAT. Two-pronged fix: 1) exempt private endpoint FQDN/IP from TLS inspection (SNI passthrough/allowlist), 2) add private endpoint IPs to firewall SNAT allowlist or adjust UDR so internal VNet traffic doesn't hairpin to firewall.
priya (networking): Workarounds we can suggest to customer now:
- Add the private endpoint IP range (10.1.12.45/32) to TLS inspection bypass.
- Add outbound rule to preserve original source (if supported) or include firewall SNAT IPs in backend allowlist.
- Remove UDR 0.0.0.0/0 for subnets calling private endpoints; use service endpoints or specific routes.
jordan (support): Quick commands we asked customer to run:
```
# verify SNI
openssl s_client -connect 10.1.12.45:443 -servername api.redwood.internal
# verify route to endpoint
ip route get 10.1.12.45
# tcpdump on firewall public SNAT ip (if possible)
tcpdump -n host <firewall-snat-ip> and port 443
```
azure-support: We reviewed firewall config. TLS inspection is enabled with a rule that matches FQDN *.redwood.internal. The firewall is proxying TLS and presenting its cert. Azure Firewall supports "Allow TLS passthrough" by disabling decryption for that FQDN or creating an exception. SNAT is happening using the firewall's SNAT public IP pool -> backend sees source X.X.X.5.
liam (sre): For long term: advise customer to use service tags or private link policies so private endpoint traffic never leaves VNet path. We should also add guidance to our docs: "Do not route PrivateLink traffic through perimeter firewall performing TLS decryption" and provide reproduced steps + commands.
jordan (support): Customer accepted bypass config and after disabling TLS decryption for the endpoint we see clean 200s from app-prod-eu-1. They also added firewall SNAT IP to backend allowlist while they adjust UDRs. Closing for now, will follow up to update docs & include a KB for Azure Firewall bypass + route examples. :white_check_mark:
priya (networking): I'll draft the KB and attach recommended az cli snippets and an architecture diagram.
liam (sre): Thanks everyone. Filing internal postmortem & doc PR. :thumbsup:
